text:
Maya (People Ops): quick Q — someone booked an intercity rail ticket to Berlin for conf and then took a Lyft from Hauptbahnhof to the hotel. Company card declined on the Lyft, so they paid with personal card. Can we reimburse both the rail + Lyft? any specific docs we need other than usual receipts?

Tony R: yes we can reimburse. ask for the rail receipt and the Lyft receipt. did the rider get a digital receipt from Lyft? usually that works.

Maya (People Ops): they have the rail e-ticket PDF and the Lyft email receipt. Lyft shows a EUR amount and a 4xx transaction id. company policy around split charges / personal card covers says submit both, right? want to confirm foreign currency conversion since card was personal.

Alex J: correct — submit both receipts. for personal-card transactions we ask for: amount, currency, merchant name, and proof of payment (card statement screenshot or Lyft confirmation). Finance needs a note about why company card declined.

Samir: also check if the ride is under the per-ride cap for taxis/ride-hailing. For conf travel we don't cover personal leisure legs, but a direct transfer from station to hotel is valid business.

Maya (People Ops): good call. can you paste the exact list of fields the expense form expects? I'll send to the traveler.

Finance Bot: Expense submission checklist (auto):
```
- Itemized receipt (PDF or screenshot) for each charge
- Proof of payment for personal-card charges (card statement screenshot with last 4 digits or Lyft confirmation email)
- Original rail e-ticket or invoice
- Currency and amount in original currency + converted USD amount
- Short note: reason for personal payment (e.g., company-card declined at checkout)
- Charge code / cost center
```

Finance Bot: For foreign currency conversions, use the conversion rate on the date of the charge (we accept bank/card statement rate or xe.com as backup). Attach conversion screenshot if using external rate.

Rebecca L: FYI if the company card declined repeatedly we should flag for travel card replacement. Also, if a card decline is merchant-specific (some EU payments block corporate BINs), file an incident with eng-fin to look at vendor blocklists.

Alex J: one nuance — if Lyft's receipt doesn't include VAT breakdown, that's OK for rides. Hotels/trains need receipts with VAT if we plan to reclaim VAT later. For trains, keep the invoice/e-ticket showing VAT if available.

Maya (People Ops): thanks. I'll message the traveler with a compact checklist and request the screenshots. also ask them to submit the expense within 7 days per policy.

Samir: small tip — if the traveler wants faster reimbursement, have them select 'Out-of-pocket (urgent)' in the expense form and tag with "people-ops:travel-urgent". Finance will prioritize small personal-card travel claims. :+1:

Maya (People Ops): perfect — sending now. anyone want to add wording I should paste?

Tony R: paste this short blurb: "Please upload the rail e-ticket and Lyft receipt, include a screenshot of the personal card statement showing the charge (last 4 digits only), and add a one-line reason: 'company card declined at point of sale'. Convert the Euro amounts to USD and attach conversion proof if not using bank rate"

Maya (People Ops): pasted and sent to traveler. thanks all :pray:
